role: Executive Director, South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department
stance_basis: two letters explicitly stating the S.C. Wildlife and Marine Resources Department opposes construction of the project
summary: James A. Timmerman, Jr., Executive Director of the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department, submitted multiple letters opposing the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project. His concerns centered on the destruction of trout streams, threats to the two-story trout fishery in Lake Jocassee, disruption of a unique spawning run in Howard Creek, inadequate data to support conclusions in the DEIS, and poor land use practices by Duke Power Company. He requested a delay in licensing and stated opposition unless additional information resolved the uncertainties.
complaint_summary: Timmerman's March 26, 1976 cover letter formally transmits his detailed comments and reiterates the department's opposition to the project due to uncertainty and the importance of the endangered resource.

statement.text:
Attached are my comments concerning the construction of the proposed Bad Creek Pump Storage Project in South Carolina by Duke Power Company (Project No. 2740).
We have had a number of discussions with Duke Power Company's environmental staff concerning the anticipated effects of this project. In every case, I have found their environmental staff to be very competent and see no need for additional outside expertise.
We have to view the project as to its effect on our wildlife resource and try to anticipate what might happen if the data is not absolute. I would strongly recommend that you closely review all available data and revisit the site before commenting on the project.
With the uncertainty surrounding this proposed project and the importance of the resource endangered by the project, the S. C. Wildlife and Marine Resources Department opposes the construction of this project at this time.
